key_insight: TEDDY is a compact pediatric transformer that learns from ICD-coded diagnostic histories to forecast disease risk and visit timing well before diagnoses appear.
clinical_relevance: This suggests pediatric EHR trajectories may help identify children at elevated risk for future conditions, including rare diseases, using far smaller models than typical foundation models.
method: Trained a 1.84M-parameter decoder transformer on ~73 million ICD-10 diagnoses from 1.6 million children.
Modeled longitudinal diagnosis sequences and visit timing using first-occurrence prediction setup.
Benchmarked against DenseNet, CNN, RNN, LSTM, and a much larger general-purpose language model.
evidence_signal: Across 797 onset-prediction tasks spanning 16 ICD-10 chapters, TEDDY achieved a median AUC of 72.0% and outperformed all same-data baselines on 96-99% of tasks, with signal still detectable more than two years before diagnosis.
watch_item: Single-institution training and imperfect calibration for median/long-tail visit intervals may limit generalizability and implementation readiness.
paper_title: TEDDY: A Pediatric Foundation Model for Risk Forewarning from ICD-Coded Diagnostic Histories
